name: IWL World Title Tournament

date.source: The fed's own founding newsletter, dated in-fiction at the top of the card.

notes: The fed's own inaugural card: an eight-man single-elimination tournament crowning the first IWL World Heavyweight Champion, opening with a Sensational Sherri in-ring segment interrupted by Brian Pillman's own storyline invasion (the Nagamachi Corporation angle). The full bracket (Luger d. Michaels, Sid d. Benoit, Cactus Jack d. Wright, Piper d. Goldust; Sid d. Luger, Cactus Jack d. Piper; Sid d. Cactus Jack in the final) survives complete in the served text; only the tournament's own champion is registered here as a billed appearance, per the mint-bar rule for entrants who are otherwise real-wrestler bycatch rather than this wing's own original material.

name: IWL Tag Team Tournament (IWL Thursday Rampage)

date.source: The fed's own founding newsletter, dated in-fiction at the top of this second card.

notes: The night after the World Title tournament: an eight-team single-elimination tag tournament crowning the first IWL World Tag Team Champions, framed by a continuing Brian Pillman/Mr. Waylon/Nagamachi Corporation angle (the Million Dollar Challenge). The full bracket (Van Dam & Williams d. the Gangstas, Raven & Dreamer d. Flair & Steamboat, Public Enemy d. the Eliminators, Owen Hart & British Bulldog d. Michaels & Perfect; Raven & Dreamer d. Van Dam & Williams, Public Enemy d. Owen Hart & British Bulldog; Public Enemy d. Raven & Dreamer in the final) survives complete in the served text; only the angle appearance is registered here, per the mint-bar rule.

name: The Second Annual Sabby Awards

date.source: The document's own dateline (Newsletter #222) and the fed's own advance announcement, posted 13 December 1997.

notes: The fed's own year-end award ceremony, twenty awards in full, in-fiction hosted by celebrity portrayals of Vince McMahon and Pamela Anderson Lee. Its emotional centre is the renaming of the fed's own top award as the Brian Pillman Franchise of the IWL Memorial Award, presented on stage to Pillman's family two months after his real-life death; the passage names his widow by her real first name, redacted here per the privacy rule (a private individual, not a participant in this fed).
